This application for Listed Building Consent is being submitted concurrently with an application for Prior Approval under Class G (Part 3, Schedule 2 of the GPDO) for the change of use of the upper floors from commercial (Class E) to two self-contained residential units (Class C3).

The physical internal alterations detailed in this LBC application are specifically required to facilitate the delivery of the residential units proposed in the Class G application. As both applications are being submitted simultaneously, the reference number for the associated Prior Approval application is not yet available, but the two should be linked for assessment purposes.

A review of the site's history indicates that the property is a Grade II listed asset that has been largely vacant in recent years, managed under a 24-hour guardian arrangement to prevent deterioration of the historic fabric. There are no other known active applications or recent demolitions on the site.
description:
The proposal seeks Listed Building Consent for internal alterations to facilitate a change of use from commercial (Class E) to a mixed-use development comprising commercial space and two self-contained residential units (Class C3).
All proposed works are strictly internal and have been designed to preserve the special architectural and historic interest of the Grade II listed building. The physical works requiring consent include:
Internal Partitioning: Installation of sensitive, lightweight internal partitioning to create the necessary residential layouts on the first, second, and loft floors.
Acoustic Upgrades: Implementation of acoustic floor and ceiling upgrades to provide required sound insulation between the retained commercial ground floor and the new residential units above.
Fire Safety: Installation of a discreet automatic fire suppression system and fire-rated internal doors to meet safety regulations for residential occupancy.
Services: Sensitive routing of internal plumbing and electrical services to support the new kitchen and bathroom facilities.
The works involve no external alterations to the elevations, masonry, or roof form, ensuring the building's contribution to the historic terrace and the wider City Road townscape is fully preserved.
